summary: The study investigates the nucleation kinetics of Ru deposited by atomic layer deposition (ALD) on silicon oxide and silicon nitride surfaces. The process involves the use of bis(ethylcyclopentadienyl)ruthenium as a precursor and O2 as a reactant. The nucleation behavior is analyzed using transmission electron microscopy (TEM) and a theoretical model is proposed to describe the nucleation kinetics based on the adsorption of the precursor and surface diffusion of deposited adatoms. The results show that the nitride surfaces significantly enhance the nucleation process compared to silicon oxide surfaces.
evidence: The nucleation behavior of Ru deposited by atomic layer deposition (ALD) using bis(ethylcyclopentadienyl)ruthenium precursor and O2 reactant is investigated as a function of the number of ALD cycles. The substrates are thermally grown SiO2, NH3 plasma-treated SiO2, and chemical vapor deposited SiNx. The nucleation of Ru strongly depends on the substrate and is much enhanced on the nitride substrates. The study also discusses the adsorption of the Ru precursor on the substrate and the surface diffusion of deposited Ru during an ALD cycle, leading to the development of a model for describing the nucleation of an ALD film at the initial stage.
